## Upper bound: a nonzero characteristic class

They proved that \(j\) absolutely continuous measures in dimension \(d=3n-2\) always admit the required partition.

An oriented affine hyperplane is represented by \((a,b)\in S^d\), with sign function \(\operatorname{sgn}(a\cdot x+b)\). The points with \(a=0\) represent constant signs. For two sign functions \(\sigma,\tau\), the test map has, for each measure \(\mu_i\), coordinates
\[
\int\sigma\,d\mu_i,\qquad
\int\tau\,d\mu_i,\qquad
\int\sigma\tau\,d\mu_i.
\]
Absolute continuity makes this map continuous, including at the constant-sign parameters.

The two antipodal actions give a vector bundle over
\(\mathbb{RP}^d\times\mathbb{RP}^d\), with top Stiefel–Whitney class
\[
[xy(x+y)]^j
\quad\text{in}\quad
\mathbb F_2[x,y]/(x^{d+1},y^{d+1}).
\]
A nonzero top class prevents a nowhere-zero section, hence forces a zero of the test map.

Because \(n\) is a power of two, the odd binomial coefficients of \((x+y)^{2n-2}\) occur exactly at even exponents. After truncation at \(d=3n-2\), precisely two terms survive:
\[
[xy(x+y)]^{2n-2}
=x^{d-2}y^d+x^dy^{d-2}\ne0.
\]
At a zero, Fourier inversion on the two signs gives all four sign-region masses equal to \(1/4\). This also excludes constant signs and parallel or coincident hyperplanes. Thus the complement really has four connected components.

Consequently,
\[
D_s\le3n-2.
\]

## Sharp lower bound: explicit covariance forms and Gaussian measures

The decisive ingredient is a construction valid for **every even \(n=2k\ge4\)**: \(2n-2\) positive-definite symmetric matrices \(\Sigma_i\) such that
\[
u^T\Sigma_i v=0\ \text{for all }i
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=0\ \text{or}\ v=0.
\]

### Constructing the forms

Identify \(\mathbb R^{2k}\) with complex polynomials of degree at most \(k-1\), and set
\[
P(t)=\prod_{r=1}^{2k-2}(t+r).
\]
For every complementary monic factorization \(UV=P\), with both degrees \(k-1\), the coefficient vectors \(U,V\) are positive and linearly independent. Thus \(U^TV>0\).

They explicitly construct a real skew-symmetric matrix \(S\) satisfying
\[
U^TSV\ne0
\]
for every such factorization. One uniform choice uses
\[
M=(2k-1)!,\qquad T=2M^2+2.
\]
Enumerate upper-triangular positions by exponents \(e=0,\ldots,\binom{k}{2}-1\), and put \(S_{ab}=T^e\), \(S_{ba}=-T^e\). Then
\[
U^TSV=\sum_{a<b}(U_aV_b-U_bV_a)T^{e(a,b)}.
\]
Its integer coefficient vector is nonzero, with coefficients bounded by \(2M^2\). The highest nonzero term dominates all preceding terms, proving nonvanishing.

With \(Q=iS\), which is Hermitian, define the symmetric real-bilinear map
\[
B(z,w)=
\left(zw\bmod P,\,
\operatorname{Re}\langle z,w\rangle,\,
\operatorname{Re}\langle z,Qw\rangle\right).
\]
Its target has real dimension \(2n-2\).

If \(B(z,w)=0\) and both inputs are nonzero, polynomial factorization forces
\(z=\alpha U,\ w=\beta V\) for complementary factors. The last two coordinates then force respectively
\[
\operatorname{Re}(\bar\alpha\beta)=0,\qquad
\operatorname{Im}(\bar\alpha\beta)=0,
\]
because \(U^TV>0\) and \(U^TSV\ne0\). This contradicts \(\alpha,\beta\ne0\).

The coordinate matrices of \(B\) include \(I\). Retain \(I\), and replace every other coordinate matrix \(H\) by \(LI+H\), choosing an integer \(L\) exceeding every absolute row sum. These matrices are positive definite by strict diagonal dominance and span the same forms. They are the required \(\Sigma_i\).

### Realizing the obstruction by Gaussians

Set
\[
d_0=3n-3=(j-1)+n.
\]
In \(\mathbb R^{j-1}\oplus\mathbb R^n\), choose \(j\) nondegenerate Gaussians with means
\[
0,e_1,\ldots,e_{j-1}
\]
in the first summand and covariances
\[
\operatorname{diag}(I_{j-1},\Sigma_i).
\]

Any quartering hyperplane bisects every Gaussian, so it passes through every mean. Therefore both hyperplanes have nonzero normals \(u,v\) lying in the last \(\mathbb R^n\).

For centered jointly Gaussian variables, quartering by their signs requires zero correlation:
\[
\Pr(X>0,Y>0)=\frac14+\frac{\arcsin\rho}{2\pi}.
\]
Thus a common quartering pair would satisfy \(u^T\Sigma_i v=0\) for all \(i\), contradicting the construction.

These are smooth, absolutely continuous counterexamples in dimension \(3n-3\). Projection gives nondegenerate Gaussian counterexamples in every smaller positive dimension: any partition downstairs would lift upstairs. Hence
\[
D_s\ge3n-2.
\]
